headline: Big money piles into Bolsonaro; Middle East ceasefire odds firm up
summary: A quiet Sunday for prices but a loud one for big bets: about $360k of large orders went on Flávio Bolsonaro winning Brazil a week before the runoff, and a single $136k bet went against Netanyahu. Ceasefire odds for Israel–Iran and US–Iran ticked up, while oil stayed near $100 and the Fed is expected to hold in October.

takeaways.lead: Whales are loading up on Bolsonaro.
takeaways.text: About $360k of large bets went on Flávio Bolsonaro winning Brazil's Oct 25 runoff, against about $80k the other way. His odds rose 4 pts today to 81%, and Lula fell to 19.5%. The single biggest order was $70k at 80¢. A close race is still the most likely result: Bolsonaro by under 4 points is 41%.

takeaways.lead: One trader bet $136k that Netanyahu won't be the next PM.
takeaways.text: Eizenkot is now the favorite at 53% (up 3 today, up 13 this week), and Netanyahu is stuck at 28.5%. Israel votes Oct 27.

The Israel–Iran ceasefire holding through Nov 30 rose 6 pts to 63%, and through Dec 31 rose 5 to 50.5%. The US–Iran ceasefire through Nov 15 is 57% (up 5). A $143k bet went on the Iranian regime NOT falling before 2027 (now 4.5%). It's calmer, but not a peace deal: Iran agreeing to end uranium enrichment fell to 3.4%.

WTI hitting $100 this month is 87.5%, basically flat today after a 51-pt jump this week. $105 is 46.5%. The US importing Russian diesel by Oct 31 collapsed 43 pts this week to 3.5%, so there's no quick supply fix.

takeaways.lead: Anthropic's IPO bounced back after Friday's drop.
takeaways.text: An Anthropic IPO closing above $1.8T rose 14 pts today to 60% (thin $274k market). An IPO by Dec 15 is 66.5% (up 5).

A Saudi–Houthi ceasefire agreement by year-end is 35% (up 12 pts this week; thin $283k market). That matters for Red Sea shipping, and large traders also sold about $44k of 'Bab el-Mandeb closed by Oct 31' (now 3.9%).

sections.title: What's new today
bullets: Serbia's parliamentary election: Vučić's party jumped 8 pts to 68.5% versus the student list at 30.5% ($1.4M market).
Albania: PM Edi Rama out in 2026 rose 8 pts to 31.5% (up 23 this week; thin market).
Alito retirement by June 2027 fell back 9 pts to 49.5%, reversing Friday's jump. Treat it as noise for now.

sections.title: Trading signals
bullets: Oil: WTI $100 in October 87.5%, $105 46.5%, $110 23%. It's a spike, not a blowout: an all-time high by March is 24%.
Fed: no change on Oct 29 is 86.5%; a December hike is 74.5%. Large traders added $10k on 'no hike in October'.
Largest company at year-end: Nvidia 67% (down 4 today), Apple 28.6%.
Bitcoin: about $60k of large bets say it won't dip to $62.5k–$65k in October.

sections.title: Wars & geopolitics
bullets: Israel–Iran ceasefire through Nov 15: 71.5% (up 4); through Dec 31: 50.5% (up 5).
US invades Iran before 2027: 14.5%. About $66k of large bets went on 'no invasion'.
Russia–Ukraine peace talks by Dec 31 fell to 29.5% (down 26 pts this week).

sections.title: Elections that move markets
bullets: Brazil (Oct 25): Bolsonaro 81% (up 4), with heavy whale buying. Watch the Brazilian real and the EWZ fund next week.
US midterms (Nov 3): a $50k bet went against a Republican sweep (that outcome is about 8.5%). Democrats take both chambers: 62.5%.

sections.title: Everyday life
bullets: Gas and heating stay expensive: oil is about 88% likely to touch $100 this month.
2026 is 80.5% likely to be the hottest year on record (up 23 pts this week).
There's still no relief from rates: no Fed cuts this year, and a December hike is likely.
